title: For Loop with Range
concept: A for loop with a range iterates over a sequence of numbers — cleaner than a while loop for counted iterations.
why: For loops eliminate the boilerplate of managing a counter variable by hand. They're safer and more readable for counted loops.
tips: `for i in 0..5` is shorter and safer than a `while` with a counter
The loop variable is immutable — you can't change `i` inside the loop
Use `for` for counted loops; use `while` for condition-based loops
common_mistakes: Thinking `0..5` includes 5 — it doesn't! Use `0..6` for 0 through 5
Trying to reassign the loop variable: `i = i + 1` inside a for loop
Using `for` when the number of iterations isn't known in advance (use `while`)
